findings.summary: In _fetch_tweet, `author: "{tweet_author}"` wraps the fetched Twitter oEmbed author_name in quotes but never routes it through `_yaml_str()` like every other field in this diff (source_url, contributor, title, arxiv_id, paper_authors all do). `tweet_author = data.get("author_name", "unknown")` is untrusted, fetched content — a display name containing a `"` (e.g. `Bob" \ninjected: value\nx: "`) still breaks out of the quoted YAML scalar and injects arbitrary frontmatter keys. This is exactly the vulnerability the brief asks to close ('all fetched metadata values are properly escaped'), and it's the one field left unfixed.

findings.summary: Bounding the collision loop with `counter < 1000` stops the potential infinite loop, but if 1000 colliding filenames already exist, the loop exits with `out_path` still pointing at an existing file (the last candidate, `..._999.md`), and the following `out_path.write_text(...)` at line 233 then silently overwrites it. That defeats the exact purpose of the 'avoid overwriting' loop in precisely the pathological case the brief asked to harden — trading a hang for silent data loss instead of failing loudly or falling back to a collision-proof name (e.g. a uuid/timestamp suffix).
